newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Storms damage crops in Yugo Vojvodina region - paper.
newsitem.headline: Storms damage crops in Yugo Vojvodina region - paper.

text.p: Heavy storms which hit nearly all of Serbia between June 17 and 22 have seriously damaged crops on around 139,000 hectares in Yugoslavia's bread-basket region of Vojvodina, Belgrade media reported on Friday.

"Based on initial, unofficial estimates and last year's prices of agricultural produce, the storms have caused damage to crops in Vojvodina worth at least 300 million dinars," Vojvodina agriculture secretary Olga Curovic was quoted by the newspaper Nasa Borba as saying.

Gale-force winds and hail, sometimes the size of chicken eggs, caused damage ranging from 10 to 100 percent of crops on an area of 139,000 hectares, or around 8.5 percent of arable land in Vojvodina, Curovic said.
The heaviest damage in the province was in the regions of Sombor, Backa Topola, Backa Palanka, Backi Petrovac, Mali Idjos, Bac and Secanj.
The extent of the damage is still being evaluated, but initial reports indicate some 30,000 ha under wheat may also have been hit by the storms.
Despite this, the wheat yield in Vojvodina is expected to meet the targetted 3.8 tonnes per hectare, Curovic said.
Vojvodina was expected to account for 1.359 million out of Yugoslavia's 1997 forecast wheat crop of 2.749 million tonnes.

According to reports from the field, some damaged maize and sugar beet areas could regenerate while some destroyed crops would be resown where possible, Curovic said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
